transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-07-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (SableGenix Infra), Laila (CTO), James (Security), Ana (PM)

Auto Summary (auto): Customer wants private networking POC to prove residency and egress controls; evaluate peering vs PrivateLink for low-latency; run throughput + tail latency benchmarks; define success criteria and timeline.

Topics (auto): POC scope, network topology, success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline, security questions.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick intros and then jump into the network topology. I'm Maya Chen from Redwood, AE, Diego and Priya are with me for the technical bits.
[00:14] Evan: Hi all, Evan here, head of infra at SableGenix. We run inference for internal annotation tooling and a small public API. Our major constraint is residency — data never leaves eu-west-1.
[00:28] Laila: Laila, CTO. Our security bar is strict: SOC2, SSO, KMS and we need egress controls.
[00:35] James: James — security engineer. We'll own the peering side and verify flow logs.
[00:40] Ana: Ana, PM, making sure the pilot has measurable success criteria so we can sign up for production.
[00:46] Diego: Great, quick agenda: confirm topology (peering vs PrivateLink), workload sizing (QPS, tokens/request), benchmarks (P50/P95/P99 latencies, tail), success criteria and timeline.

[00:58] Maya: One note, we also support Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private — for this POC we're focusing on a Private control plane with an in-region data plane in eu-west-1. Some of the product names might get mangled in the transcript, but Diego will detail the runtime.
[01:15] Diego: On the runtime — it's our GPU-optimized serving, continuous batching and KV cache. For benching, typical metrics to capture: requests per second, average tokens per request, tokens generated per second, and latency at 50/95/99 percentiles. For LLMs we also look at cold-start regen and KV cache hit rate.
[01:40] Evan: Our baseline traffic is about 180 QPS peak for the annotation service, but that's bursty; steady-state maybe 30-40 QPS. Typical payloads are 150-400 tokens in, 50-200 tokens out.
[01:56] Ana: Timeline wise we want a proof in 4-6 weeks max, ideally 3 weeks.
[02:02] Maya: Ok, realistic pilot plan is 2 phases: Phase 1 — 7-10 day in-region functional bench with test peering/Privatelink to validate connectivity and measure latency. Phase 2 — 2-week production-simulated run with your sample traffic and SLO verification.
[02:18] Laila: On topology — we're leaning to PrivateLink because we prefer endpoint isolation, but peering looks simpler and cheaper. We need to understand tradeoffs: performance, egress control, and ops complexity.
[02:32] Diego: Right, quick tradeoff callout: VPC peering tends to give slightly lower latency because it's just routed (assuming inter-region not involved) but it can expose broader network surface and you need route management. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives strong isolation and easier policy enforcement, but can add a small NAT/ENI hop, adding ~5-15ms depending on cloud. Those numbers are fuzzy — we'll run targeted bench to quantify.
[02:58] James: Also, we have strict egress constraints — all outbound must go to specified IP ranges and go through our NAT gateway. Can Redwood's setup be restricted to only talk via privatelink endpoints?
[03:10] Priya: Yes, Redwood Private supports endpoint-only egress; we can lock down the control plane and expose data plane via interface endpoints. We'll need your subnet/CIDR ranges and we can configure security groups to only accept specific ENIs.
[03:25] Evan: What's the expected 95th percentile latency for our workloads? We need under 200ms P95 for the annotation microservice to stay usable.
[03:33] Diego: For small prompt sizes (<=200 tokens in/out) with warmed KV cache, we typically see P95 in the 80-160ms range on our ded-optimized stacks for gpt-ish models. For larger prompts or cold cache it increases. For your sizes, target P95 < 200ms is achievable but depends on batching, instance type, and if you accept quantization.
[03:57] Laila: Cost is also a factor — we don't want to pay 3x for a narrow latency gain. Can the pilot report cost-per-1k-tokens estimates?
[04:06] Maya: Yes we can produce cost estimates using Redwood Optimize profiles and also run bench to produce per-token estimates. We'll include cost delta for PrivateLink vs peering (NIC charges, data transfer).
[04:18] Ana: Success criteria proposal: (1) P95 latency <200ms for baseline prompt set; (2) stable throughput at 150 QPS for 10 minutes without queueing; (3) KV cache hit rate > 70% for stateful flows; (4) no egress to outside eu-west-1; (5) security checklist items validated (SAML SSO, KMS, flow logs).
[04:38] Diego: Sounds reasonable. I'd add a P99 cap for critical paths e.g. P99 < 500ms for interactive flows.
[04:45] Evan: We also need reproducible benchmark artifacts — you run with our traffic and share raw results and the bench script.
[04:52] Diego: We'll share the bench scripts and a spreadsheet with P50/P95/P99 and cost columns. We'll tag runs with model name, sequence length config, batching window, and whether KV cache was used.
[05:06] Ana: For region locking, we need proof that logs and any persisted artifacts don't leave eu-west-1. How does Redwood Private handle audit logs and telemetry?
[05:16] Priya: With Redwood Private the control plane can be in your VPC or we can run a customer-managed control plane. Audit logs for the data plane can be routed to your Kinesis/S3 in-region; we support pushing flow logs and inference logs to your bucket, encrypted with your KMS. We'll include an architecture diagram showing log flows.
[05:36] James: We will require a signed DPA and explicit data retention settings for the POC.
[05:40] Maya: Noted — I'll attach the DPA template and policy options.
[05:44] Evan: Network specifics: our infra team prefers peering for performance but we're open to testing PrivateLink if we see measurable difference. We can open a test VPC and share peering routes. We also run strict NACL rules.
[05:58] Diego: For benching we'll run two topologies: (A) VPC peering with routed path from your app subnet to our data plane subnet in eu-west-1; (B) PrivateLink interface endpoints with security groups restricting ingress. We'll measure raw RTT, request latency at different concurrent levels (10, 50, 150 QPS), and cost.
[06:18] Laila: What's realistic on the timeline to stand up endpoints? We can give subnets and the test account now.
[06:24] Maya: If we get subnet details this week we can provision test endpoints in 2-3 business days. Diego's bench run will take another 3 days to iterate, then Phase 2 2 weeks. So the overall end-to-end pilot from kickoff ~21-28 days if both sides move quickly.
[06:40] Ana: Do you need any sensitive data? We'll sanitize payloads but we want bench to reflect real token distributions.
[06:47] Diego: Realistic token distribution is important; sanitized but representative prompts are fine. Also we prefer a mix of single-turn and multi-turn flows so KV cache behavior is exercised.
[06:58] James: On compliance, how do you handle key management? Our KMS is customer-managed; we need to ensure model state or logs aren't encrypted with Redwood keys.
[07:08] Priya: You can bring your own KMS for S3 buckets and for disk encryption on the VMs. For ephemeral caches we don't persist kv to S3 unless configured; if you need, we can route any persisted artifacts to your bucket.
[07:22] Maya: Quick note about canary/fallbacks — in the pilot we'll test a fallback policy to a slightly cheaper quantized model if latency spikes. That will be part of the cost/quality tradeoff analysis.
[07:33] Evan: We want to avoid model quality regressions. How will you measure output fidelity?
[07:38] Diego: We'll run your eval set with human-eval labels if you provide them, plus automatic metrics (response similarity, BLEU-ish token overlap for structured tasks). We'll correlate any quantized model runs with a delta threshold: if quality drops >2% on your eval metric we flag it.
[07:58] Ana: Ok, recap and next steps?
[08:01] Maya: Recap: Redwood to share security docs + architecture, SE to run bench, customer to provide sample traffic and subnets, run two topology tests (peering vs PrivateLink), capture P50/P95/P99 and cost, and meet in two weeks to review results.
[08:16] Laila: We need a calendar invite for the review and the DPA before any real data leaves our staging environment.
[08:22] Maya: I'll send both today.
[08:25] (brief cross talk)
[08:33] James: One last nit — ensure VPC flow logs show no unexpected egress to non-eu addresses during the bench. We'll validate with our SIEM.
[08:40] Priya: We'll provide flow logs, and Diego will annotate the bench runs with the capture times so you can cross-check.
[08:48] Evan: Thanks everyone, this feels actionable.
[08:52] Maya: Great, thanks for your time. We'll follow up with the whitepaper and the invite.
[08:58] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcription: some technical terms may be transcribed imperfectly (eg 'K V cache' instead of 'KV cache', 'Redwood Dedicate' instead of 'Redwood Dedicated', 'Private link' sometimes split). There are a few overlaps and filler words preserved to keep authenticity.

Bench plan (brief text in transcript):
- Bench 1 (connectivity test): ICMP and TCP RTT from app subnet to data plane across peering and privatelink, measure jitter over 10k samples.
- Bench 2 (latency/throughput): synthetic workload at 10/50/150 QPS for 10 minutes each, capture P50/P95/P99, queueing, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.
- Bench 3 (production sim): run customer sample traffic for 48 hours to surface tail behaviors, collect logs and costs.

Success criteria (reiterated in transcript):
- P95 < 200ms for target prompt set
- Stable 150 QPS for 10 minutes with no request queueing >500ms
- P99 < 500ms for interactive flows
- KV cache hit > 70% for multi-turn flows
- No egress outside eu-west-1; flow logs validated

Files to be shared after call (as recorded in transcript):
- Redwood Private network whitepaper (link)
- SOC2 summary + DPA template (link)
- Benchmark spreadsheet and bench scripts (link after run)
- Pilot calendar invite and topology playbook (link)

End of transcript
